methodological_rigor.justification: Well-designed spatial proteomics study with 82 BCG-treated NMIBC samples analyzed via imaging mass cytometry. Rigorous cohort selection with transparent exclusion criteria (n=6 excluded for technical quality only, not clinical characteristics). Stratified train-test split at patient level maintains independence. Two complementary analytical approaches (single-cell phenotyping and CNN-GA-MIL) with appropriate controls. Limitation: test set very small (n=10, 5 responders/5 nonresponders); authors acknowledge findings as exploratory requiring validation in larger cohorts.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Cohort study of high-risk NMIBC patients treated with BCG (gold-standard therapy). Study addresses critical clinical question: predicting BCG response to optimize treatment decisions. Spatial immune profiling and AI classifiers could guide personalized therapy. However, findings currently exploratory; predictive model tested on only 10 patients limits immediate clinical translation. Validation in larger independent cohorts required before clinical implementation.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods comprehensively described for IMC staining protocol and cell segmentation. ARRIVE elements partially addressed (study population, objectives clear; complete reporting of statistical methods and exclusion details provided). Limitations: IMC raw images and processed segmentation data availability not explicitly stated; CNN-GA-MIL model code/weights not mentioned as shared. Hyperparameter details and training specifics somewhat sparse.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel application of imaging mass cytometry combined with AI (gated attention multiple instance learning) to predict BCG response in NMIBC. Spatial single-cell characterization at high resolution (40-marker detection) previously limited in bladder cancer. Identification of stromal (fibroblast, plasma cell) and immune phenotypes associated with BCG failure substantively advances mechanistic understanding. First study to apply IMC-specific CNN-based learning to this clinical question in bladder cancer.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear, well-organized manuscript with logical flow from clinical motivation through methods to results. Figures effectively communicate spatial cell distributions and model performance. Mathematical notation for indices (II, TT, IT) well-defined. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within prior bladder cancer literature and acknowledges exploratory nature. Tables effectively summarize clinical characteristics and IMC findings. Accessible to both computational and clinical readers.

key_strengths: Novel integration of high-dimensional spatial proteomics (IMC) with AI-based prediction model for BCG response prediction
Rigorous cohort selection with transparent technical exclusion criteria and appropriate train-test split strategy
Two complementary analytical approaches (spatial phenotyping and CNN-GA-MIL) provide biological and computational perspectives
Clinically actionable findings identifying BCG-nonresponder phenotypes enriched in immunosuppressive fibroblasts and plasma cells
key_concerns: Test set very small (n=10) for model validation; 90% accuracy claim requires confirmation in larger independent cohorts
Model generalizability unclear; single-center cohort may not capture broader NMIBC heterogeneity
IMC data availability and CNN-GA-MIL code/weights not stated as accessible; reproducibility unclear
Findings appropriately labeled exploratory by authors; premature clinical implementation would be inappropriate without larger validation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically sound spatial proteomics study with novel AI application. Appropriate for Tier 2 with minor revisions pending: (1) explicit commitment to larger validation study; (2) statement of data/code availability; (3) clarification of model generalizability limitations.
